_note: KSP1PartMod animation settings. enabled: master switch for KSP1 animations. fix_mu_reader: patch Redux's .mu reader so models of format version 0 to 2 load (false leaves Redux untouched). own_first_deployable: remove Redux's deployable module from the part and let KSP1PartMod play that clip too. follow_redux_deployables: Redux keeps the state of a part's single deployable (and of parachutes) but its Mecanim copy of the clip does not move; KSP1PartMod draws the clip from Redux's state (false leaves those clips still). hide_material_less_renderers: hide the renderers of KSP1 parts whose materials are all missing (drawn with Unity's error colour). fix_part_icons: light KSP1 part icons: give the icon subject the rendering layers of the icon studio's lights (false keeps Redux's black icons). editor_animation_speed: speed of KSP1 animations in the VAB, times the flight speed: 1 = real speed (default, smooth), 1000 = instant, 0 = KSP1's own editor values (x10 for doors and panels, gear and legs instant). shader_property_map: KSP1 material property -> KSP2 property names to try, in order; when present it replaces the built-in map. subcategory_bar: in the VAB, a second vertical bar of KSP1 part types (Pods, Engines, Robotics...) next to the category bar when a KSP1 mod category is selected (false removes it). diagnostics: log once, in the VAB, the materials of a few KSP1 parts (lines '[KSP1PartMod] diag:'), for bug reports. material_curves: play the material colour and value curves of KSP1 clips (engine glow, lights, windows); false keeps them still, as before. light_curves: play the light curves of KSP1 clips (intensity, colour, range, spot angle) on lights that Redux does not drive. emission_setup: when a KSP1 glow is written to a KSP2 material whose emission is switched off, give that renderer its own material copy with emission on, and a white emission map when it has none (false leaves the materials as they are). throttle_effects: let FXModuleThrottleEffects drive the colour changers of its engine with the throttle (BDB engine glow). heat_glow: play KSP1's heat glow (Heat entries and their curves); set false if KSP2 already makes hot parts glow. skip_modules: list of KSP1 module names KSP1PartMod never takes, for example ["FXModuleThrottleEffects"], to switch one module off if it misbehaves. plugin_modules: animate the KSP1 plugin modules that Redux leaves still: engine nozzle extensions (DeployableEngines, Bluedog_DB), the multi-mode nozzle, look-at pistons, animated decouplers, RCS glow, mesh hiders, DMagic science booms (visual only, no science), the acceleration spring and the Mercury landing bag (false leaves them still, as in 0.4.0; skip_modules also names them). b9_module_gates: a B9PartSwitch subtype that switches a module off (moduleActive = false) also switches off the animation entries of that module, whatever their kind, following the variant chosen on the part; the gates apply to all our entries, phase 1 kinds included (false animates every module whatever the variant). perf_counter: log every 60 s the time spent by KSP1PartMod's animations (lines '[KSP1PartMod] anim: perf:'), for bug reports about performance. fix_fairing_init: let Redux finish setting up the jettison shroud (Module_Fairing) of KSP1 engines, which otherwise breaks them in the VAB (red cylinder left, part that cannot be picked again): an empty list of base colliders instead of a missing one, and no shroud colour set on parts without colours (false leaves Redux as it is). engine_tooltip_stats: show the max thrust, Isp and propellant of KSP1 engines in the VAB tooltip, as for KSP2 engines (false leaves the tooltip as Redux makes it). subcategory_bar_keeps_grid: while the sub-category bar is shown, widen the parts panel by the bar's width so the third column of parts is not cut (false narrows the grid instead, as in 0.4.0). share_ksp1_textures: load each KSP1 texture file once and share it between every KSP1 part that uses it, instead of one copy per part each time Redux rebuilds a part (less video memory: an estimate from reading Redux's code, not measured yet; the 'textures:' lines below give the real figures; false keeps one copy per part, as in 0.4.0). ksp1_textures_follow_quality: let the KSP1 textures that Redux keeps readable follow the game's Texture Quality setting (most KSP1 textures are not readable: Unity cannot lower them once loaded, they stay at full size either way). raise_streaming_budget: off by default; raise the game's texture streaming budget by the memory the KSP1 textures take, so KSP2 textures keep their resolution, capped at the video card's memory less a quarter (at least 1 GB); can cause stutter on cards with little memory. Lines '[KSP1PartMod] textures:' in the log give the texture memory at the end of the import and at each VAB or flight entry. ksp1_engine_shrouds: keep the KSP1 mesh of engine shrouds (ModuleJettison) and show it the way KSP1 does, instead of Redux's Module_Fairing, which cannot size or colour it: the shroud shows while a part is attached below the engine (in the VAB and in flight), follows the chosen part variant, and goes away on decoupling (or on staging for an engine that is not a fairing); it has no mass, drag or debris; it acts only when enabled is true (false gives the behaviour of 0.6.0, Redux's Module_Fairing included). audit_on_vab_entry: off by default; when true, the first time you enter the VAB in a game session KSP1PartMod loads every KSP1 part once, off screen and one at a time, and writes a report (audit-<date>.csv and .md in the mod folder audit/) of the parts that fail, throw, stay unfinished or log errors; it changes nothing in your craft (a part that crashes the game is skipped at the next run). audit_frame_budget_ms: time the audit may use per frame, in milliseconds (default 8, 1 to 50). audit_unload_every: number of parts between two unloads of the audit's textures (default 100, 10 to 1000). ModuleManager patches (applied by Redux when it imports KSP1 parts; nothing is written to the cfg files): mm_plugin_safety_net: KSP1 plugins (DLLs) never run under Redux, so a plugin's folder proves nothing: the names below are treated as absent, :NEEDS[name] is false and :NEEDS[!name] is true, and the patches written for them (:FOR[name], :BEFORE[name], :AFTER[name], and the patches inside that folder) are left out; parts are never removed (false: Redux's rule, a folder of that name counts as present). mm_plugin_folders: the plugin names always treated as absent (RealFuels, FAR, Kerbalism, TweakScale...); add or remove a name here. mm_plugin_folders_auto: also treat as absent every KSP1 folder that holds a .dll and no part. mm_needs_keep: names never treated as absent, even with a .dll (B9PartSwitch, Waterfall and the libraries whose behaviour Redux or KSP1PartMod reproduces). mm_before_after_need_mod: as ModuleManager does, leave out a patch whose :BEFORE[name] or :AFTER[name] names a mod that is not there (a :FOR name counts as there; :LAST patches are always kept). mm_arithmetic: apply ModuleManager's *=, +=, -= and /= on values (Redux skips them; ^= and != stay skipped); a value that is not a single number is left as is. mm_index_selectors: apply ModuleManager's ,n ,-n and ,* after a value or node name (@volume,1 edits the second volume only; Redux edits them all). mm_edit_first_match: off by default; when true, an edit without an index changes the first match only, as ModuleManager does (false: every match, as Redux does). Lines '[KSP1PartMod] mm:' in the log count what each of these changes.

shader_property_map._note: The first name the material has is used. _EmissionColor comes first: it is the emission property seen on the KSP2 shaders of KSP1 parts in game.
